questions.question: 1. Which one of the following tasks is most suitable for RNNs?

explanations.a: Incorrect because image classification is mainly handled by CNNs.
explanations.b: Correct because RNNs are widely used for sequence tasks such as text generation.
explanations.c: Incorrect because reinforcement learning is a learning paradigm, not a primary RNN purpose.
explanations.d: Incorrect because object detection is a computer vision task.

questions.question: 2. What is the main characteristic of a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)?

answers.a: It processes data sequentially and has loops in its architecture
answers.b: It processes data in parallel and has no loops
answers.d: It is designed for image classification

explanations.a: Correct because feedback loops enable sequence modelling.
explanations.b: Incorrect because that describes feedforward networks.
explanations.c: Incorrect because RNNs can have multiple layers.
explanations.d: Incorrect because CNNs are used for images.

questions.question: 3. Which layer type is typically used to capture sequential dependencies in an RNN?

explanations.a: Incorrect because the input layer only receives data.
explanations.b: Correct because the hidden layer maintains memory across time steps.
explanations.c: Incorrect because the output layer produces predictions, not dependencies.
explanations.d: Incorrect because activation layers add non-linearity but do not store sequence information.

questions.question: 4. What is the advantage of using recurrent layers in an RNN?

answers.a: They can capture temporal dependencies in the input data
answers.b: They process all inputs simultaneously in parallel

explanations.a: Correct because recurrent connections allow learning from past inputs.
explanations.b: Incorrect because RNNs process sequences sequentially, not in parallel.
explanations.c: Incorrect because data generation is an application, not an inherent advantage.
explanations.d: Incorrect because non-linearity comes from activation functions, not recurrence.

questions.question: 5. What is the purpose of the hidden state in an RNN?

answers.a: To store the information from the previous time step
answers.b: To adjust the learning rate during training
answers.c: To compute the gradients for backpropagation

explanations.a: Correct because hidden state carries memory forward.
explanations.b: Incorrect because learning rate is controlled by the optimizer.
explanations.c: Incorrect because gradients are computed during backpropagation.

questions.question: 6. Why do Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) share parameters across time steps?

answers.a: To allow the model to learn different features at each step
answers.b: To increase the total number of learnable parameters
answers.c: To enable the network to generalize across sequences of varying lengths
answers.d: To eliminate the need for an activation function

explanations.a: Incorrect because sharing parameters means applying the same feature extraction everywhere.
explanations.b: Incorrect because parameter sharing drastically reduces the total number of parameters.
explanations.c: Correct because applying the same weights at every step allows the model to handle sequences of any length.
explanations.d: Incorrect because activation functions are still needed for non-linearity.

questions.question: 7. What does the number of time steps in an unrolled RNN correspond to?

answers.a: The number of hidden layers in the network
answers.b: The total number of parameters in the network
answers.c: The length of the input sequence being processed

explanations.a: Incorrect because unrolling creates a sequence of identical layers, not deep hidden layers.
explanations.b: Incorrect because parameters are shared, so the number of parameters doesn't scale with time steps.
explanations.c: Correct because an RNN is unrolled once for each element in the input sequence.
explanations.d: Incorrect because the output classes are determined by the output layer, independent of time steps.

questions.question: 8. What is a common challenge when training standard Recurrent Neural Networks on very long sequences?

answers.a: The network learns to process data too quickly
answers.b: The vanishing or exploding gradient problem
answers.c: The inability to use any activation functions
answers.d: The requirement to have a fixed input size

explanations.a: Incorrect because training on long sequences typically slows down the process.
explanations.b: Correct because gradients can diminish or grow uncontrollably when backpropagated through many time steps.
explanations.c: Incorrect because activation functions are still used.
explanations.d: Incorrect because RNNs naturally handle variable-length inputs.

questions.question: 9. What is the main difference between an RNN and a feedforward neural network?

explanations.a: Incorrect because convolution layers are used in CNNs, not RNNs.
explanations.b: Correct because RNNs contain recurrent (feedback) connections that allow information to persist across time steps.
explanations.c: Incorrect because RNNs can have one or more hidden layers.
explanations.d: Incorrect because RNNs are mainly used for sequential data such as text and time series.

questions.question: 10. What dataset is commonly used for character-level language modelling demonstrations?

explanations.a: Incorrect because MNIST is a handwritten digit image dataset, not used for text modelling.
explanations.b: Incorrect because CIFAR-10 is an image classification dataset.
explanations.c: Incorrect because ImageNet is used for large-scale image recognition tasks.
explanations.d: Correct because Tiny Shakespeare is widely used for character-level language modelling with RNNs.
